An initial GC filing has been created for a project. Plumbing work for the same construction project and property will be filed later, potentially by a different applicant.

Should the plumbing scope receive a new unrelated job number or a subsequent filing under the existing job?

answer.answerText:
The plumbing scope should be filed as a subsequent (S) filing under the existing GC job number, rather than as a new unrelated job number, if it is part of the same construction project and property. DOB guidance says all filings for the same construction project should use the same job number with an extension; a subsequent filing adds new scope of work and work types, and it may use a new/different applicant. It is separately processed and may be permitted before the initial GC filing. [DOB NOW application user guide, p. 5](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/dob_now_application_user_guide.pdf#page=5)

For submission, the initial GC filing must first be submitted—not remain in pre-filing status. The FAQ says a subsequent filing can then be initiated and submitted until an LOC has been issued for the initial filing. The guide directs users to select “Subsequent Filing” from the Filing Action column beside I1. The materials acknowledge that a subsequent can be created before I1 is submitted, but its populated fields will not update until I1 is submitted; they do not fully resolve any broader rule on creation timing before I1 submission. [DOB NOW application user guide, p. 6](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/dob_now_application_user_guide.pdf#page=6) [DOB NOW: Build FAQs — Subsequent Filings](https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/industry/dob-now-build-faqs.page)

Completion handling depends on the initial job type. The general guidance says an LOC is requested separately for each initial and subsequent filing. But for NB or Alteration-CO filings, the specialized FAQ says not to request an LOC for the subsequent filing: its status remains Permit Entire, while only I1 changes to CO issued. The initial job type was not supplied, so this completion branch cannot be selected here. Subsequent applications are strongly encouraged. All filings with the same job number will go to the same plan examiner or team and the Records Management Fees are paid on the initial filin g only. (Yes = Alteration CO) • Alteration is a major chan ge to exits? (Yes = Alteration CO) • Alteration in number of stories? (Yes = Alteration CO if Building Type is 3 Family or Other) Full Demolition - The dismantling, razing, or removal of all of a building or structure, including all related incidental opera tions. DOB NOW: Build Frequently Asked Questions > Subsequent Filings — When can I submit a subsequent job filing? — Subsequent filings can be initiated and submitted after the initial job filing is submitted (not in pre-filing status). Users no longer have to wait until the initial filing is approved. A subsequent filing can be submitted anytime until an LOC has been issued for the initial filing.

DOB NOW: Build Frequently Asked Questions > Subsequent Filings — Do I have to request a Letter of Completion (LOC) for a subsequent job filing? — Yes, an LOC needs to be requested for each filing, initial and subsequent filings.

DOB NOW: Build Frequently Asked Questions > Subsequent Filings — If an initial job application is filed as professional certification can the subsequent application be filed as a standard plan filing type? — Yes, initial and subsequent jobs can have different filing types.

DOB NOW: Build Frequently Asked Questions > Subsequent Filings — Can a subsequent filing have a different design applicant than the initial filing? — Yes, the applicant on an initial filing and a subsequent filing can be different. If the applicant is the same, one application can be submitted if the work types are eligible to be combine filed.

DOB NOW: Build Frequently Asked Questions > Subsequent Filings — Do I have to pay the record management fee on a subsequent filing? — No, the $165 record management fee is now charged only once on the initial filing and is no longer a fee on subsequent filings.

DOB NOW: Build Frequently Asked Questions > Subsequent Filings — Can I have an open PAA for the initial filing and a subsequent filing at the same time? — Yes.

DOB NOW: Build Frequently Asked Questions > Subsequent Filings — How can I make a minor change to a legalization filing? — Post-Approval Amendments (PAA) are not allowed on filings that include legalization work. If a change needs to be made, a subsequent filing will be required or the job must be withdrawn and refiled. For Boiler Equipment filings the only option is to withdraw and refile the job. In addition, permits cannot be renewed if the job includes legalization work.

DOB NOW: Build Frequently Asked Questions > Subsequent Filings — I have a subsequent filing in pre-filing status and some of the fields are grayed out? How do I complete these fields? — Fields from the subsequent filing are populated from the initial filing (I1). The fields will not update on the subsequent filing until the I1 is submitted. To prevent this issue, we recommend completing as much of the I1 as possible before creating the subsequent filing.

DOB NOW: Build Frequently Asked Questions > New Building and Alteration-CO — Do I need to request a Letter of Completion for the subsequent filing of an NB or Alteration-CO filing? — No, the status of the subsequent filings will remain Permit Entire. Only the status of the initial (I1) filing will change to CO issued. If a Temporary CO is issued, the status of the initial job will remain Permit Entire until the Final CO is issued.

Section PC 202: General Definitions ACCEPTED ENGINEERING PRACTICE. That which conforms to accepted principles, tests or standards of nationally recognized technical or scientific authorities. ACCESS (TO). That which enables a device, fixture, appliance or equipment to be reached by ready access or by a means that first requires the removal or movement of a panel, door or similar obstruction (see "Ready access (to)"). ACCESS COVER. A removable plate, usually secured by bolts or screws, to permit access to a pipe or pipe fitting for the purposes of inspection, repair or cleaning. ADAPTER FITTING. An approved connecting device that suitably and properly joins or adjusts pipes and fittings that do not otherwise fit together . AIR BREAK (Drainage System). A piping arrangement in which a drain from a fixture, appliance or device discharges indirectly into another fixture, receptacle or interceptor at a point below the flood level rim and above the trap seal. AIR GAP (Drainage System). The unobstructed vertical distance through the free atmosphere between the outlet of the waste pipe and the flood level rim of the receptacle into which the waste pipe is discharging. AIR GAP (Water Distribution System). The unobstructed vertical distance through the free atmosphere between the lowest opening from any pipe or faucet supplying water to a tank, plumbing fixture or other device and the flood level rim of the receptacle. ALTERNATIVE ENGINEERED DESIGN. A plumbing system that performs in accordance with the intent of this code and provides an equivalent level of performance for the protection of public health, safety and welfare. The system design is not specifically regulated by this code. ANCHORS. See "Supports." ANTISIPHON. A term applied to valves or mechanical devices that eliminate siphonage. AREA DRAIN. A receptacle designed to collect surface or storm water from an open area. ASPIRATOR. A fitting or device supplied with water or other fluid under positive pressure that passes through an integral orifice or constriction, causing a vacuum. Aspirators are also referred to as suction apparatus, and are similar in operation to an ejector. BACKFLOW. The undesirable reversal of flow of water or mixtures of water and other liquids, gases or other substances into the distribution pipes of the potable supply of water from any source or sources or the undesirable reversal of flow from the intended direction of flow in the drainage system due to a system stoppage, system overload or a higher pressure on the drainage pipe side of the house trap. Backpressure, low head. A pressure less than or equal to 4.33 psi (29.88 kPa) or the pressure exerted by a 10-foot (3048 mm) column of water. Backsiphonage. The backflow of potentially contaminated water into the potable water system as a result of the pressure in the potable water system falling below atmospheric pressure of the plumbing fixtures, pools, tanks or vats connected to the potable water distribution piping. Drainage. A reversal of flow in the drainage system. Water supply system. The flow of water or other liquids, mixtures or substances into the distribution pipes of a potable water supply from any source except the intended source. BACKFLOW CONNECTION. Any arrangement whereby backflow is possible. BACKFLOW PREVENTER. A backflow prevention assembly, a backflow prevention device or other means or method to prevent backflow into the potable water supply. BACKWATER VALVE. A device or valve installed in the building drain, sewer or any branch line where such drain or branch is subject to backflow, and which prevents drainage or waste from backing up into a lower level or fixtures and causing a flooding condition. BALL COCK. See "Fill Valve." BASE FLOOD ELEVATION. Refer to Section G201.2 of Appendix G of the New York City Building Code . BATHROOM GROUP. A group of fixtures consisting of a water closet, lavatory, bathtub or shower, including or excluding a bidet, an emergency floor drain or both. Such fixtures are located together in the same room. A fixture designed to wash bedpans and to flush the contents into the sanitary drainage system. Any part of the piping system that extends to fixtures on two or less consecutive floors except a riser, main or stack. BRANCH INTERVAL. That portion of a drainage system that does not drain by gravity into the building sewer. BUILDING TRAP. CIRCUIT VENT. A vent that connects to a horizontal drainage branch and vents two traps to a maximum of eight traps or trapped fixtures connected into a battery. CISTERN. 403.3 403.3 Required employee and public toilet facilities. Employees shall be provided with toilet facilities in all occupancies. The number of plumbing fixtures located within the required employee toilet facilities shall be provided in accordance with Section 403 for all employees. Customers, patrons and visitors shall be provided with public toilet facilities in structures and tenant spaces intended for public utilization. The number of plumbing fixtures located within the required public toilet facilities shall be provided in accordance with Section 403 for all customers, patrons and visitors. Employee and public toilet facilities may be separate or combined. Where combined facilities are provided, the number of plumbing fixtures shall be in accordance with Section 403 for all users. Exception: Public utilization of toilet facilities shall not be required for: 1. Food service establishments, as defined in Section 81.03 of the New York City Health Code , with a seating capacity of less than 20, provided such establishments are less than 10,000 square feet (929 m 2 ). 2. Establishments less than 10,000 square feet (929 m 2 ) classified as Occupancy Group B or M pursuant to Sections 304.1 and 309.1 of the New York City Building Code, respectively, provided however that this exception shall not apply to a building or nonaccessory tenant space used for assembly purposes by fewer than 75 persons and classified as a Group B occupancy in accordance with Section 303.1.2 of the New York City Building Code .

102.2 102.2 Existing installations. Except as otherwise specifically provided, plumbing systems lawfully in existence on July 1, 2008 or on the effective date of a subsequent amendment of this code shall be permitted to have their use and maintenance continued if the use, maintenance or repair is in accordance with the original design and no hazard to life, health or property is created by such plumbing system.

401.1 401.1 Scope. This chapter shall govern the materials, design and installation of plumbing fixtures, faucets and fixture fittings in accordance with the type of occupancy, and shall provide for the minimum number of fixtures for various types of occupancies.

1301.1 1301.1 Scope. The provisions of Chapter 13 shall govern the materials, design, construction and installation of systems for the collection, storage, treatment and conveyance of nonpotable water. The use and application of nonpotable water shall comply with the New York City Construction Codes , and all applicable laws, and rules, including but not limited to those of the Department of Environmental Protection and the Department of Health and Mental Hygiene. Water from nonpotable systems shall be collected, stored, treated, conveyed and used on the same tax lot unless otherwise approved by the commissioner. The following water recycling uses are not addressed in this chapter: 1. Rainwater collected utilizing a retention system through rain barrels complying with the requirements of the Department of Environmental Protection; 2. Commercial car washing facilities; and 3. Water closet-sink combinations. A fixture that enables wastewater from a lavatory to discharge directly into the flushing tank of a water closet may be utilized provided it complies with the New York City Construction Codes , including all accessibility requirements. The water closet and lavatory shall be located in the same room.

108.4.1 108.4.1 New, altered, extended or repaired systems. New plumbing systems and parts of existing systems that have been altered, extended or repaired shall be tested as prescribed herein to disclose leaks and defects, except that testing is not required in the following cases: 1. In any case that does not include addition to, replacement, alteration or relocation of any water supply, drainage or vent piping. 2. In any case where plumbing equipment is set up temporarily for exhibition purposes. 3, For ordinary plumbing work, the department may accept written certification from a licensed master plumber that the job was performed in compliance with the requirements of this code and rules of the department. 4. Minor alterations and ordinary repairs. 5. In accordance with the exceptions in Section 312.1.

403.1.1 403.1.1 Fixture calculations. To determine the occupant load of each sex, the total occupant load shall be divided in half. To determine the required number of fixtures, the fixture ratio or ratios for each fixture type shall be applied to the occupant load of each sex in accordance with Table 403.1 . Fractional numbers resulting from applying the fixture ratios of Table 403.1 shall be rounded up to the next whole number. For calculations involving multiple occupancies, such fractional numbers for each occupancy shall first be summed and then rounded up to the next whole number. Fixture calculations in Group B office occupancies shall utilize the total occupant load on a given floor to determine the number of fixtures required for that floor. Exception: The total occupant load shall not be required to be divided in half where approved statistical data indicates a distribution of the sexes of other than 50 percent of each sex.

403.2 403.2 Separate facilities. Where plumbing fixtures are required, separate facilities shall be provided for each sex. Exceptions: 1. Separate facilities shall not be required for dwelling units and sleeping units. 2. In structures or tenant spaces where combined employee and public toilet facilities are provided in accordance with Section 403.3, separate facilities shall not be required where the total number of employees, customers, patrons and visitors is 30 or fewer. 3. In structures or tenant spaces where required toilet facilities for only employee use are provided in accordance with Section 403.3, separate facilities shall not be required where the total number of employees is 30 or fewer. 4. In structures or tenant spaces where required toilet facilities for only public use are provided in accordance with Section 403.3, separate facilities shall not be required where the total number of customers, patrons and visitors is 30 or fewer.

403.2.1 403.2.1 Family or assisted-use toilet facilities serving as separate facilities. Where a building or tenant space requires a separate toilet facility for each sex and each toilet facility is required to have only one water closet, two-family* or assisted-use toilet facilities shall be permitted to serve as the required separate facilities. 419.2 419.2 Substitution for water closets. In each bathroom or toilet room, urinals shall not be substituted for more than 50 percent of the required water closets.

Post Approval Amendment (PAA) > The PAA Process – DOB NOW: Build Job Filings — The following rules apply to PAA filings in DOB NOW: Build : — • Only one PAA can be in progress at a time. • A PAA can only be filed by an Applicant of Record . • A PAA must be filed by the same Applicant of Record as the original filing. • A PAA cannot be submitted if the filing includes legalization. • The description of the changes must be entered in Plans/Work (PW1) tab – Comments. • A flat, one-time fee of $100 is charged when a new PAA is filed. • An increase or decrease in the estimated job cost results in a recalculation of fees. Post Approval Amendment (PAA) > The PAA Process – DOB NOW: Build Job Filings > Step 1: Log In to DOB NOW: Build — • Use the log in information that is registered in eFiling to log into DOB NOW: Build.

Post Approval Amendment (PAA) > The PAA Process – DOB NOW: Build Job Filings > Step 2: Locate Job Filing — • Locate the approved initial job filing on your dashboard in DOB NOW: Build . • Initiate the PAA. System generates filing number for the PAA. • Amend the necessary information.

Post Approval Amendment (PAA) > The PAA Process – DOB NOW: Build Job Filings > Step 3: Upload Required Documents — • Upload revised PDF of the plan sets. • Upload DPL1 document. • The system will determine if additional documents are required based on the information that is data entered on the PAA job filing.

Post Approval Amendment (PAA) > The PAA Process – DOB NOW: Build Job Filings > Step 4: Obtain Attestation — • Applicant, owners and other stakeholders must electronically sign the job filing.

Post Approval Amendment (PAA) > The PAA Process – DOB NOW: Build Job Filings > Step 5: Submit payment — • Payments will be made online using a credit card, debit card or e-check. • Anyone associated to a job filing can submit a payment.

Post Approval Amendment (PAA) > The PAA Process – DOB NOW: Build Job Filings > Step 6: Preview to File — • Applicant must review the filing and provide a final electronic signature.

Post Approval Amendment (PAA) > The PAA Process – DOB NOW: Build Job Filings > Step 7: Submit Job Filing — • Applicant must officially electronically submit the job filing to the Department.

Include a description of the changes in the Comments field (Section 24) of the Plans/Work tab (PW1).

"},{"spanIndex":9,"text":"For Standard Plan Examination filings, a complete plan set needs to be uploaded if changes are being made to the approved plans. "},{"spanIndex":10,"text":"Submit the new unapproved sheets with no approved stamp and include the previously approved plans with a DOB stamp. "},{"spanIndex":11,"text":"The new unapproved sheets should indicate the P1 suffix on the filing extension, however, the approved plans with a DOB stamp should not be changed. "},{"spanIndex":12,"text":"Once the PAA is approved, the new plan set uploaded will replace the previous plan set for the filing. "},{"spanIndex":13,"text":"If no changes are being made to the plans, then a new plan set is not required with the PAA; select No to the question, Are you submitting updated plans?
"},{"spanIndex":14,"text":"
"},{"spanIndex":15,"text":"DOB NOW: Build Frequently Asked Questions > Post Approval Amendments — Is fee estimation for additional filing fees associated with PAAs done automatically in DOB NOW? — Yes. "},{"spanIndex":16,"text":"If the cost/scope of the job changes resulting in additional fees, the PAA will collect those automatically and payment must be made online before submitting the PAA.
"},{"spanIndex":17,"text":"
"},{"spanIndex":18,"text":"DOB NOW: Build Frequently Asked Questions > Post Approval Amendments — Can I change the owner on a PAA? — No. "},{"spanIndex":19,"text":"Owner changes are done through a supersede request. "},{"spanIndex":20,"text":"The new owner can log into DOB NOW: Build , Search by Job Number, and from the Filing Action select Supersede and then Owner. "},{"spanIndex":21,"text":"Select the Owner Type and then Save the request. "},{"spanIndex":22,"text":"If the owner type is not fee exempt, select the Pay Now button to pay the $130 fee. "},{"spanIndex":23,"text":"Then the Applicant of the job needs to log into DOB NOW and complete the Statements & Signature section. "},{"spanIndex":24,"text":"Then the new owner can also complete the Statements & Signature section and submit the request.
"},{"spanIndex":25,"text":"
"},{"spanIndex":26,"text":"DOB NOW: Build Frequently Asked Questions > Post Approval Amendments — Is owner’s signature required on a PAA? — Yes, in DOB NOW the questions on the Owner’s Attestation section can be changed with a PAA so the owner must provide a signature again in this section to submit the PAA.
"},{"spanIndex":27,"text":"
"},{"spanIndex":28,"text":"DOB NOW: Build Frequently Asked Questions > Post Approval Amendments — Where do I file a post approval amendment (PAA) on an existing BIS OT/GC, Alt-1 or NB job? — OT/GC filings in D status or later by December 23, 2020 and Alt-1 or NB jobs in D status or later by February 26, 2021 will continue to be processed in BIS. "},{"spanIndex":29,"text":"PAAs on existing BIS filings will continue to be filed in BIS.
"},{"spanIndex":30,"text":"
"},{"spanIndex":31,"text":"DOB NOW: Build Frequently Asked Questions > Post Approval Amendments — Do I need to upload an AI1 form with the plans to explain the changes in the PAA? — Do not upload an AI1 form with the plans when doing a PAA. "},{"spanIndex":32,"text":"Use the Comments field (Section 24) in the PAA filing to provide a description of the changes.
"},{"spanIndex":33,"text":"
"},{"spanIndex":34,"text":"DOB NOW: Build Frequently Asked Questions > Post Approval Amendments — Can I request a sign-off for a PAA? — No. "},{"spanIndex":35,"text":"PAAs are filed to update the information on an initial filing. "},{"spanIndex":36,"text":"The filing status of a PAA will always remain Approved."}]},{"passageIndex":2,"sourceID":"dob-application-guide","claimID":"official-passage-789cc7ccd439eb8374132031","contentHash":"9befc1cc76dd0efbfb76fed2960c262f1c4a61fc8dd786f9c30341251cc852b5","spans":[{"spanIndex":0,"text":"Page 5 of 38
"},{"spanIndex":1,"text":"JOB FILING /APPLICATION
"},{"spanIndex":2,"text":"A job is an application submitted for a construction project on a property, which can vary from making alterations to a single unit in an
"},{"spanIndex":3,"text":"existing building or to constructing a new building with many units. "},{"spanIndex":4,"text":"A job filing/application is submitted to obtain a Work Permit to
"},{"spanIndex":5,"text":"perform a specific type of construction.
"},{"spanIndex":6,"text":"All filings related to the same construction project should have the same job number and then an alphabetic and numeric extension that
"},{"spanIndex":7,"text":"indicates the filing type and sequence: I - Initial, S - Subsequent, and P - Post Approval Amendment (PAA).
"},{"spanIndex":8,"text":"• Initial Filings (I1) – The first or initial job filing created for a construction project .
"},{"spanIndex":9,"text":"• Subsequent (S) - A subsequent filing is an additional filing under the same job filing number that allows an applicant (the same one
"},{"spanIndex":10,"text":"on the initial or a new applicant) to add new scope of work and new work types to a job on the same property. "},{"spanIndex":11,"text":"A subsequent filing
"},{"spanIndex":12,"text":"can have a different review type (standard plan examination/professional certification) than the initial filing. "},{"spanIndex":13,"text":"Once submitt ed, a
"},{"spanIndex":14,"text":"subsequent filing functions as a separate appli cation. "},{"spanIndex":15,"text":"It can be permitted before the initial is permitted and a Letter of Completion
"},{"spanIndex":16,"text":"(LOC) is requested separately on each filing.
"},{"spanIndex":17,"text":"• Post Approval Amendment s (PAA) - A Post Approval Amendment or PAA is for making changes to a filing after it has been approved.
"},{"spanIndex":18,"text":"To create a job fi ling , log into DOB NOW: Build and from the dashboard select +Job Filing . "},{"spanIndex":19,"text":"Then select the Job Type , Work Type (s) , and
"},{"spanIndex":20,"text":"Filing Review Typ e .
"},{"spanIndex":21,"text":"Subsequent applications are strongly encouraged. "},{"spanIndex":22,"text":"All filings with the same job number will go to the same plan examiner or team and the
"},{"spanIndex":23,"text":"Records Management Fees are paid on the initial filin g only. "},{"spanIndex":24,"text":"It is also beneficial to have one job number to connect all of the work on a
"},{"spanIndex":25,"text":"project."}]},{"passageIndex":3,"sourceID":"dob-application-guide","claimID":"official-passage-99e3ff631d01ad61590ccecf","contentHash":"9befc1cc76dd0efbfb76fed2960c262f1c4a61fc8dd786f9c30341251cc852b5","spans":[{"spanIndex":0,"text":"Page 13 of 38
"},{"spanIndex":1,"text":"Filing Review Type
"},{"spanIndex":2,"text":"Standard Plan Examination or Review – submission of an application subject to t he Department’s standard examination process for plan
"},{"spanIndex":3,"text":"review and approval .
"},{"spanIndex":4,"text":"Professional Certification – s ubmission of application s, which are a ccepted with no Department examination , based on the professional
"},{"spanIndex":5,"text":"certification of an applicant who is a Registered Design Professional (RDP) stating that the filing is in compliance with all applicable laws.
"},{"spanIndex":6,"text":"Professional ly c ertified p lans are subject to an audit by the Department of Buildings.
"},{"spanIndex":7,"text":"The Job Type, Work Type and Filing Review Type cannot be changed once it is selected and submitted.
"},{"spanIndex":8,"text":"See the Filing Statuses Guide for a complete list of review statuses for both DOB NOW and BIS jobs. "},{"spanIndex":9,"text":"The status bar on a filing indicates
"},{"spanIndex":10,"text":"the pr ogress of the filing with a blue circle. "},{"spanIndex":11,"text":"A white check mark will appear in the circle once the stage has been completed by DO B and
"},{"spanIndex":12,"text":"the filing has moved on to the next step in the filing process. "},{"spanIndex":13,"text":"A red exclamation point will appear to indicate that the fili ng is waiting for
"},{"spanIndex":14,"text":"action by the applicant because DOB has issued Objections or the filing is in QA Failed status. "},{"spanIndex":15,"text":"Once the filing is complete, white check
"},{"spanIndex":16,"text":"marks will appear in all the circles on the status bar. "},{"spanIndex":17,"text":"If the filing is a PAA, an approval is indica ted by a solid blue circle without a check
"},{"spanIndex":18,"text":"mark."}]},{"passageIndex":4,"sourceID":"dob-application-guide","claimID":"official-passage-ce20f813e92241a7bc12804a","contentHash":"9befc1cc76dd0efbfb76fed2960c262f1c4a61fc8dd786f9c30341251cc852b5","spans":[{"spanIndex":0,"text":"Page 16 of 38
"},{"spanIndex":1,"text":"Stakeholders
"},{"spanIndex":2,"text":"All stakeholders require an eFiling account. "},{"spanIndex":3,"text":"Visit www.nyc.gov/efilin gtips for more information. "},{"spanIndex":4,"text":"All grayed - out fields will auto - populate with
"},{"spanIndex":5,"text":"information from the eFiling account.
"},{"spanIndex":6,"text":"Applicant and Owner: Enter the email address associated with the eFiling account of the Applicant and Owner . "},{"spanIndex":7,"text":"In most cases, the Applicant is a
"},{"spanIndex":8,"text":"Registered Architect or Professional Engineer. "},{"spanIndex":9,"text":"For the Applicant, also select the License Type and Business Name. "},{"spanIndex":10,"text":"For the owner, select the Owner
"},{"spanIndex":11,"text":"Type. "},{"spanIndex":12,"text":"If the Owner Type selected is Non - Profit Organization, NYC Agency, O ther Government Owned or NYCHA/HHC, then the fees will be removed
"},{"spanIndex":13,"text":"and an ACRIS report is required to verify the building is tax exempt.
"},{"spanIndex":14,"text":"Filing Representative and Delegated Associates : An email address can also be entered for Filing Representative Class I/ Preparer and Delegated
"},{"spanIndex":15,"text":"Associates (Filing Representative Class II or Other Licensee).
"},{"spanIndex":16,"text":"Filing Review Type, Work Type /Filing Includes
"},{"spanIndex":17,"text":"The Filing includes – select if the application is for New Work or Legalization . "},{"spanIndex":18,"text":"This option cannot be changed once the filing fees are paid.
"},{"spanIndex":19,"text":"If Legalization is selected and there is no OATH summons on the BIN for work without permit (WWP), then a $600 or $6000 fee, depending on the
"},{"spanIndex":20,"text":"building type, is added to the filing fees as a legalization fee. "},{"spanIndex":21,"text":"If legalization is selected and an OATH summons number for WWP is on the BIN,
"},{"spanIndex":22,"text":"select Yes to the question Are there any OATH/E CB summonses related to this work? "},{"spanIndex":23,"text":"and enter the DOB violation or OATH/ECB Summons
"},{"spanIndex":24,"text":"number(s). "},{"spanIndex":25,"text":"When a WWP violation is entered, there is no legalization fee and only a civil penalty for work without permit cal culated as an L2 fee.
"},{"spanIndex":26,"text":"An L2 is a request for ove rride, reduction or waiver of civil penalties for work without a permit violations. "},{"spanIndex":27,"text":"When the L2 request is created, the civil
"},{"spanIndex":28,"text":"penalty fee has to be paid before the permit is issued. "},{"spanIndex":29,"text":"Once legalization is selected on a filing, it results in a no work pe rmit and Post Approval
"},{"spanIndex":30,"text":"Amendments are not allowed. "},{"spanIndex":31,"text":"See 1 RCNY 102 - 04 (b) (7 ) for more information about legalization and civil penalties.
"},{"spanIndex":32,"text":"The work is being done to legalize work without a permit listed as a violating condition in a Request for Corrective Action ( RCA) issued by DOB?
"},{"spanIndex":33,"text":"– if Yes is selected, provide the complaint number of the RCA. "},{"spanIndex":34,"text":"See 1 RCNY 102 - 06 and the September 2021 Service Notice for information about the
"},{"spanIndex":35,"text":"Homeowner Relief Program.
"},{"spanIndex":36,"text":"Filing Review T ype - auto - populated based on the selection made when creating the application and cannot be changed.
"},{"spanIndex":37,"text":"The below selections are auto - populated based on the selection made when creating the application but can be changed in this section:
"},{"spanIndex":38,"text":"Is this Application for a Small Business?
"},{"spanIndex":39,"text":"Is this Application for an approved project under the M ajor Project Developments Program (MPP) ?"}]}]}}
